title: Hosted Inference v4 — Adaptive Quantization & Fallback: Release Notes
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This document summarizes the Hosted Inference v4 release (rolling deployment beginning 2029-03-22). v4 introduces two tightly integrated features designed to reduce unit cost without compromising availability or customer-facing quality: Adaptive Progressive Quantization (APQ) and Policy-driven Fallback Routing (PFR). The release also adds token-level traces to the Console, new SLO adjustments for quantized variants, and an upgrade/rollback playbook for customers and operators.

Highlights

- Adaptive Progressive Quantization (APQ): dynamic, per-tenant quantization profiles that progressively apply lower-precision kernels during low-quality-risk windows and revert automatically when quality regressions are detected.
- Policy-driven Fallback Routing (PFR): per-route routing policies to fail over from a primary model variant to one or more compatible variants (quantized or alternative-size models) with configurable latency and fidelity budgets.
- Token‑level cost traces and streaming flags in Redwood Console for precise cost attribution and debugging.
- New SLO / billing mapping guidance for quantized variants and fallbacks.
- Operator upgrade and rollback playbook and automated canary rollout pipeline.

Why this release

Customer feedback and internal analysis showed that many production workloads could accept limited fidelity fluctuation to gain substantial cost savings. However, customers wanted built-in safety: predictable fallbacks, observability to understand cost-quality tradeoffs, and smooth upgrade processes. v4 addresses this by coupling automated quantization with conservative, policy-driven fallbacks and observability.

Detailed feature descriptions

1) Adaptive Progressive Quantization (APQ)

Short summary: APQ introduces runtime profiles that apply increasingly aggressive quantization to model execution paths when monitored quality signals remain within tolerances. Profiles are tenant-scoped and adhere to guardrails defined by product and research.

Behavioral rules (high level):
- Start in baseline (FP16/int8 hybrid) for new requests.
- If recent closed-loop eval metrics (prompt-set pass rates, perplexity deltas, user-reported quality) are stable for configured window (default 60m), shift to next quantization tier (e.g., int8 -> int4-fp8 hybrid).
- Continuously monitor evaluation metrics and automatic regression detectors; revert to the last safe tier on regression.
- Per-route override allowed: customers may pin routes to disallow quantization.

APQ configuration table (defaults shown)

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|
| enable_apq | true | Master switch per tenant |
| evaluation_window | 60m | Rolling window for metric aggregation |
| pass_rate_threshold | 0.98 | Minimum pass-rate to advance tier |
| max_tier | 2 | Maximum aggressive tier applied (0=baseline) |
| revert_grace_period | 10m | Minimum time after revert before re-attempt |

Notes:
- "Pass-rate" is computed against tenant-provided or Redwood-supplied prompt checks. Tenants can attach custom prompt-sets via the Console.
- APQ is powered by a lightweight online evaluator; historical logs are retained for 30 days by default.

2) Policy-driven Fallback Routing (PFR)

Short summary: PFR allows customers and operators to declare fallback chains and fidelity budgets per route. The PFR engine will route requests to compatible variants when primary capacity is constrained or SLOs are at risk.

Key primitives:
- route_policy (json): ordered list of candidate variants and routing conditions.
- fidelity_budget: per-route token or latency budget that bounds fallback duration.
- regional_affinity: controls whether fallbacks may move cross-region.

Example route_policy (Console JSON snippet):
{
  "primary": "redwood/gptx-13b-fp16",
  "fallbacks": [
    {"variant": "redwood/gptx-13b-int8", "max_latency_ms": 250},
    {"variant": "redwood/gpt-7b-int4", "max_latency_ms": 150}
  ],
  "fidelity_budget_tokens_per_hour": 500000
}

Routing rules summary:
1. Prefer primary variant while latency and error budget are healthy.
2. If latency SLO breach or primary capacity shortage detected, attempt first-compatible fallback.
3. Do not exceed fidelity_budget for more than the configured window (default 1h).
4. Fallback may be disabled for regulated routes via per-tenant policy.

Observability additions

- Token-level cost traces: per-request breakdowns showing kernel execution time, batch impact, and quantization tier. Visible in Console under Requests -> Traces.
- Quality guardrail dashboards: prompt-set pass rate, rolling A/B comparison between quantized and baseline variants.
- New telemetry labels: apq_tier, fallback_reason, fidelity_budget_used.

SLOs and economic impact

- Baseline latency SLOs remain unchanged for primary variants. Quantized variants may have lower latency; customers can opt to adjust per-route SLOs.
- Typical cost reductions observed in internal benchmarks: 20–45% CPU/GPU cost reduction for suitable workloads at tier 1–2 quantization.

SLO impact table (expected, internal guidance):

| Metric | Primary variant | Quantized Tier 1 | Quantized Tier 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p95 latency (1k seq) | 120ms | 95ms | 85ms |
| cost per token | 1.00x | 0.80x | 0.60x |
| expected quality delta | 0% | -0.8% | -1.6% |

Upgrade and migration guidance

This section describes steps for both Redwood operators and customers to adopt v4 features.

Operator canary rollout (internal):
1. Deploy APQ and PFR to canary cluster (region-us-central-canary) with apq.enable=false globally.
2. Run internal canary traffic and run automated regressions (sampled prompt-sets).
3. Flip apq.enable for 5 pilot tenants with diverse workloads. Monitor pass_rate and latency for 24 hours.
4. Expand to 20% of production traffic, then 50%, then global, respecting revert criteria.

Customer self-serve migration (recommended):
1. Preview: enable APQ in Console "Preview" mode for selected routes (no automatic tier advancement; telemetry only).
2. Configure tenant prompt-set and quality thresholds.
3. Enable APQ with max_tier=1 and fidelity_budget conservative value (e.g., 100k tokens/hour).
4. Monitor Quality Guardrail dashboards for 72h. If stable, increase max_tier or fidelity_budget.
5. Consider enabling PFR for high-availability routes; set regional_affinity to "preferred" or "strict" depending on compliance needs.

Breaking changes and compatibility notes

- Default increased telemetry: additional request metadata will be logged for tenants that opt-in to APQ. Customers concerned about log volume can disable detailed traces per route.
- Older SDKs (pre-2028-09) will not expose the apq_tier and fallback_reason fields in streaming responses. Upgrade to the latest SDK for full feature access.

Known issues and mitigations

- Intermittent false-positive regressions in particular long-tail prompt-sets. Mitigation: extend evaluation_window for affected tenants to 180m and provide manual holdback.
- Some extremely latency-sensitive customers observe worse p50 with aggressive fallback chains due to cross-variant cold-starts. Mitigation: pin routes to single-variant or pre-warm fallbacks.

Telemetry retention and privacy

- APQ evaluation logs: retained 30 days by default. Operators can request extended retention for enterprise accounts.
- Fallback traces: retained per customer tenancy and exported to customer-owned S3 on request for compliance cases.

Rollout timeline and calendar

- 2029-03-22: v4 feature flag rollout begins (internal canaries).
- 2029-04-03: first gated expansion to pilot tenants.
- 2029-05-01: general availability for all Hosted API tenants.

- Support playbook: see related runbook at sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/rolling-upgrades-and-fallbacks-runbook.json

Appendix: quick CLI snippets

Enable APQ for tenant (Console CLI):
redwoodctl tenant update --tenant-id=tenant_123 --set apq.enable=true --set apq.max_tier=1

View recent APQ regressions (Console API):
GET /api/v1/tenants/tenant_123/apq/regressions?since=2029-03-01

Contact and escalation

For production regressions or unexpected customer impact, open a P1 with SRE and tag: "apq-impact". Follow the incident playbook: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/apq-and-fallback-incident-playbook.json

End of release notes.
